overview: The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) is a Government of India initiative under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) to promote apprenticeship training and provide financial support to establishments engaging apprentices. It aims to bridge the skill gap by offering stipend support to apprentices and incentivizing industries to participate in skill development. NAPS operates through a digital portal for registration, contract management, and reimbursement processes, targeting youth and establishments across India.
objectives: Provide financial support to establishments engaging apprentices
Bridge the skill gap between education and industry requirements
Increase youth employability through on-the-job training
Support implementation of the Apprentices Act, 1961
Enable digital processing of apprenticeship contracts and claims
Encourage industry participation in skill development initiatives
eligibility: Establishments covered under the Apprentices Act, 1961 are eligible to engage apprentices and claim reimbursement under NAPS. Candidates must meet the educational and age criteria specified for the designated or optional trade they are applying for. Establishments must have a valid registration on the apprenticeship portal and comply with contract signing, advisor verification, and payroll creation timelines as per portal guidelines.
benefits: Financial reimbursement of stipend paid to apprentices (up to prescribed limits), facilitation of apprenticeship contracts through a digital portal, access to a wide range of training courses across sectors, support for Basic Training Providers (BTPs), and integration with schemes like PMKVY and NCVT for auto-population of candidate data. Non-financial benefits include skill development, improved employability, and industry-institute linkage.
financial_support: Under NAPS, the government reimburses 25% of the prescribed stipend subject to a maximum of Rs. 1,500 per month per apprentice for a maximum period of 500 hours of basic training. Reimbursement is processed through the apprenticeship portal after contract approval by the Apprenticeship Advisor and verification of stipend payment by the establishment. The stipend for apprentices is paid by the establishment, and the government provides partial reimbursement as per the scheme norms.
application_process: 1. Establishments register on the apprenticeshipindia.org portal. 2. Candidates register as apprentices on the portal. 3. Establishment selects a candidate and issues a contract through the portal. 4. Candidate signs the contract within 7 days of issuance. 5. The signed contract is routed to the Apprenticeship Advisor for verification/approval within 30 days. 6. Upon approval, stipend payroll is created and establishment pays the apprentice. 7. Establishment submits reimbursement claim through the portal for government share of stipend. 8. Claims are processed and funds transferred to the establishment's registered bank account.
required_documents: Certificate of Incorporation or registration proof
Special board resolution (for companies changing name)
Document of transfer duly signed (for business transfer)
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)
contact_details: Email: vs.arvind@nic.in | Helpline: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence
caveats: Reimbursement under NAPS is not available for extended training periods due to lockdown if stipend was not paid during the pause
Online training proposals under consideration do not qualify for NAPS reimbursement
Backdating of termination date is not allowed for contracts enjoying NAPS benefits
Portal will not accept termination requests if remaining training period is ≤ 45 days
Establishments must maintain 100% profile completion to issue contracts
Candidates must complete profiles to apply for apprenticeships
